findings.title: Hero's "Taxes & deductions" chip can show a bigger deduction than the gross next to it, and disagrees with the Breakdown a tap away
findings.where: index.html:3487 (hero chip renders calc.ded) and index.html:1244-1250 (computeNet)
findings.detail: computeNet() computes `ded = pretax+fica+fed+st+posttax+cw` uncapped (line 1244) and returns it as `ded`, but then deliberately caps the *displayed* pre/post fields (`dispPre`/`dispPost`, lines 1246-1249) specifically 'so Breakdown rows still sum' when a period's gross can't absorb the full flat pretax/posttax deductions. The hero's chip at line 3487 (`Taxes & deductions –{fmt(calc.ded)}`) is the one and only other consumer of `.ded` in the whole file (confirmed by grep) and uses the raw uncapped value, so it never got the same treatment.
findings.failure: Any signed-in nurse who has entered a per-period Pre-tax or Post-tax deduction in Settings (a completely normal, first-class field, not an edge feature) and views a pay period where she hasn't logged shifts yet -- the default state at the start of every new two-week period, or right after finishing Settings before adding a single shift -- sees a hero that reads e.g. 'Projected take-home $0' with chips 'Gross $0' next to 'Taxes & deductions –$260' (reproduced exactly: pretaxDeductions=200, posttaxDeductions=60, gross=0 -> ded=260, net=0). Tapping 'See the full breakdown' immediately shows every row at $0, summing correctly to gross. The two on-screen surfaces for the identical pay period visibly disagree about how much was withheld, which reads as a broken calculator on the app's single core promise -- know what a shift is worth, no surprises -- and is reachable through completely ordinary use, not a contrived input.
findings.fix: Render the hero's deduction chip as `calc.gross-calc.net` (or equivalently the sum of the already-capped fields computeNet returns: fica+fed+st+cw+pre+post) instead of the raw `calc.ded`, so it is definitionally reconciled with the net figure right next to it and with the Breakdown view. This is a one-line change at the App component's JSX call site (line 3487) and does not require touching computeNet's return shape since `.ded` has no other reader.

findings.title: Every per-shift/day "before you work it" preview (Add-Shift, calendar tiles, weekend-pickup suggestion, goal shift-count) uses a flat keepRatio approximation that silently ignores percent-type custom withholdings, while the hero/Breakdown use the real computeNet math that does account for them
findings.where: index.html:2818-2820 (keepRatio definition) used at 3434, 3919, 3933, 4104-4105/4245-4246, and Settings 4746
findings.detail: `keepRatio = Math.max(0, 1-(federalTaxRate+stateTaxRate+ficaForPreview)/100)` (2819-2820) is the marginal take-home ratio used for every *individual* shift/day figure shown before a shift is committed: the Add-Shift sheet's 'This shift adds ... take-home' preview (4104-4105, 4245-4246), the 'Pick up a weekend night?' suggestion (3434, 3512), every calendar day tile's ~$ amount and aria-label (3919, 3933), and the Settings goal line's '≈ N typical 12h shifts to reach this' (4746, `per = baseRate*12*keepRatio`). It correctly omits flat-dollar pretax/posttax/custom deductions (those don't scale with one more shift, so excluding them from a marginal ratio is right), but it also omits `customWithholdings` entries of type `'percent'`, which computeNet (1243) *does* apply proportionally to every dollar of gross -- so they should be part of the marginal rate too. Verified: a shift priced at $600 gross with a 5% percent-type custom withholding plus 12% federal/5% state/7.65% FICA previews as +$452 take-home via keepRatio but nets only +$422 once actually computed via computeNet -- a 7% systematic overstatement that recurs on every shift with that data shape, silently, with no hedge beyond the generic 'about'.
findings.failure: A nurse with a percent-type custom withholding configured (e.g. an extra state withholding percentage, a percent-based garnishment or retirement match modeled that way) would see every pre-commit preview -- the number the whole app exists to get right -- consistently promise more take-home than what actually lands in the hero/Breakdown once the shift is added, which is exactly the class of surprise the product is built to prevent.
findings.fix: Fold each percent-type entry in customWithholdings into keepRatio's subtraction the same way fed/state/fica already are, e.g. `keepRatio = 1 - (federalTaxRate+stateTaxRate+ficaForPreview+percentCW)/100` where percentCW sums `customWithholdings.filter(w=>w.type==='percent').map(w=>+w.amount||0)`. Low severity because this data shape currently has no Settings UI to create it at all (grep confirms `customWithholdings`/`setCW` is only read from Export/Import JSON and the paystub scanner never populates it -- verified in parsePDF/applyPaystub, lines 3333-3383) -- today it is unreachable through normal in-app use, so flag it as a latent bug that will bite the moment that field gets a Settings affordance, not an active one.

findings.title: Saved templates silently drop the Overtime flag, so reusing one understates the shift's value with no on-screen signal
findings.where: index.html:4140-4160 (doSaveTemplate builds `tpl` without isOvertime), :4135-4139 (applyTemplateTap never sets isOvertime on the shift it inserts), :2915-2926 (toggleQuickFillDay same), :1051-1068 (templates sanitizeData branch has no isOvertime field at all)
findings.detail: The template object model has no isOvertime field anywhere in its lifecycle: doSaveTemplate's `tpl = {name, shiftType, hours, bonusType, customBonus, ...start}` (line 4154) never reads it, even though the same function goes out of its way (comment at 4144-4150) to correctly recover bonusType/customBonus/start from the just-added list entry so the template 'faithfully captures what's on the day.' Both places a template is turned back into a shift -- applyTemplateTap (4136) and quick-fill's toggleQuickFillDay (2922) -- construct the new shift object without an isOvertime key, so it's always falsy. The templates branch of sanitizeData (1051-1068) also has no isOvertime coercion, confirming this isn't a one-off omission but the actual data shape.
findings.failure: A nurse configures Night 12h + Overtime + On-call bonus (base $40, night diff $10/hr -> $50/hr differential rate). The live preview correctly shows 1.5x972 + 60 = about $1,032 take-home-adjusted gross, she clicks '+ Add to this day', then immediately 'Save as template' (e.g. named 'Mandatory OT night'). Any later use of that template -- the one-tap 'QUICK ADD FROM TEMPLATE' chip in the sheet, or bulk quick-fill across days on the calendar -- adds a shift worth only base+diff x12 + bonus (about $708, 31% less), because isOvertime is silently false. Nothing in the UI discloses this: the per-shift row in 'ON THIS DAY' (4192-4202) shows no dollar figure at all, so there's nothing to contradict the number she remembers from when she built the template, and no toast/label ever says 'overtime not saved to templates.' This directly breaks the promise of knowing what a shift is worth before working it -- the number she believes she reproduced isn't the number she'll actually get.
findings.fix: Include isOvertime in the tpl object doSaveTemplate builds (mirroring how it already recovers src.bonusType/src.start), set it on the shift objects applyTemplateTap and toggleQuickFillDay construct, and add `isOvertime: t.isOvertime===true` to the templates sanitizeData coercion so it round-trips through storage. If dropping OT from templates is actually intentional, the QUICK ADD/quick-fill chip should say so or omit the OT-looking styling, rather than silently producing a lower number.

findings.title: The 'live' shift-value preview doesn't update while typing custom Hours or a custom Bonus amount -- only on blur
findings.where: index.html:4016-4035 (NumInput buffers keystrokes in local `raw` state and only calls onCommit on blur or Enter), consumed by Hours at :4226 and Custom bonus at :4241, feeding previewGross/previewNet at :4104-4105 and the preview block at :4243-4249
findings.detail: NumInput's onChange only updates its own local `raw` string; the value it hands back to AddShiftSheet (and thus `hours`/`customBonus` state, and therefore previewGross/previewNet) only changes in the onBlur/Enter commit handler. Every other control in the sheet (hour-preset buttons, shift-type chips, the Overtime toggle, the bonus <select>) updates the preview the instant it's clicked, but the two free-text numeric fields do not.
findings.failure: A nurse is offered a 10-hour pickup with a $200 flat incentive and wants to see if it's worth it before committing. She taps the Hours field and types '10' (replacing the default 12), then taps the Bonus dropdown to 'Custom' and types '200' into the amount field. If she reads the 'This shift adds +$X gross ... take-home' line at that point -- exactly the moment the feature exists to answer -- it still reflects the pre-edit 12h/$0-bonus shift, because neither keystroke has been committed yet. The number only becomes correct once she taps/tabs to another field. Anyone who trusts what's on screen at the moment of decision, rather than blurring the field first, is shown a stale figure for exactly the two most decision-relevant customizable inputs (hours and a flat bonus).
findings.fix: Either have NumInput report a best-effort parsed value on every keystroke (falling back to the last committed value on unparseable input, e.g. '1.') so previewGross/previewNet track it live like every other control, or have AddShiftSheet read the field's in-progress text directly for the preview calculation while it's focused.

findings.title: "Take-home per paycheck" is a cycle-average, shown with full confidence, for the exact rotations where real paychecks diverge from it
findings.where: patternMetrics index.html:1257-1299 (comment at 1253-1256); displayed unqualified in PatternLab at index.html:4428 (compare table), 4447 (pattern card), 4540-4542 (edit-mode money block)
findings.detail: patternMetrics averages gross/net over lcm(cycle,14) days and divides by (span/14) periods to get periodGross/periodNet/periodHours (1294-1298). The average of a real 14-day paycheck window over a periodic on/off sequence is invariant to which phase of the cycle a given real paycheck lands on ONLY when the cycle length divides 14 evenly (i.e. cycle ∈ {2,7,14} within the allowed 2..42 range) — because only then does every non-overlapping 14-day window contain the same whole number of full cycles. For every other cycle length — which includes the built-in 'weekend'-adjacent choice of 28 days in PATTERN_CYCLE_CHOICES (1146) and, most visibly, the shipped preset '4 on, 4 off nights' (id 4on4off, cycle:8, index.html:1163-1164) — consecutive real 14-day paychecks contain a DIFFERENT number of actual shifts depending on where the cycle's phase falls, so the true paychecks alternate above and below the displayed average rather than matching it. Concretely, for the 4on4off preset with the app's own default baseRate 65.15 and night differential +10 (index.html:2204, 688), a 12h night shift grosses 75.15*12=$901.80 (shiftGross, 1125-1133). Over the lcm(8,14)=56-day span (4 periods) the real per-period shift counts are 8,8,6,6 (28 total, matching 7 cycles * 4 shifts/cycle) — i.e. real paychecks alternate between ≈$7,214 and ≈$5,411 gross (a ~$1,800 swing), while the lab shows one flat number: the average of those, ≈$6,313. Every actual paycheck a nurse who applies this pattern receives will be either noticeably higher or noticeably lower than the number she was shown before committing to the rotation — exactly the kind of surprise the app's whole premise ("know what a shift is worth before it's worked") exists to prevent. The code's own comment at 1254-1256 calls this averaging 'an honest per-paycheck figure,' but nothing in the UI tells the user it's an average: the yearly figure is explicitly hedged with '≈' (line 4542, '≈ {fmt(metrics.yearNet)} a year') while the much more decision-relevant per-paycheck figure right next to it, and in the pattern list card and side-by-side comparison table, carries no such hedge anywhere.
findings.failure: A nurse opens Pattern lab, picks the built-in '4 on, 4 off nights' preset (or types a custom 28-day cycle), sees 'Take-home per paycheck: $X' with no qualifier, and applies it to her calendar planning around that number. Her first real paycheck comes in ~$900-1,800 different (net) from what she was shown, with no warning that the number she budgeted against was ever anything but a fixed promise for every check.
findings.fix: Qualify periodNet/periodGross/periodHours the same way yearNet already is — at minimum prefix them with '≈' in all three surfaces (index.html:4428, 4447, 4540-4542) whenever metrics.drifts is true or, more precisely, whenever cycle length doesn't evenly divide 14, and add one line under the money block naming that real paychecks will alternate (e.g. 'averaged — cycles that don't line up with a 2-week pay period pay more some checks and less others'). This is a display-only change in PatternLab and doesn't require touching patternMetrics's math, though a stronger fix (surfacing the actual min/max per-period swing) would.

findings.title: Welcome-screen sample take-home figure is hardcoded and doesn't match the app's own math for the identical schedule
findings.where: index.html:5721-5722 (welcome screen literal) vs sampleNet() at index.html:3416-3423, DIFF_DEFAULTS at index.html:686-697, default baseRate at index.html:2204
findings.detail:
The obStep===0 welcome screen shows a static, non-computed figure: `
Sample · 72 hrs this period
` followed by `
$3,951
` (line 5721-5722) — literal strings, not derived from any function. The same '72 hrs / 6 shifts' scenario is independently defined a few hundred lines later in `sampleNet()` (3 night + 2 weekend-day + 1 base, 12h each = 72 hrs), which the 'done' screen (obStep 4) actually renders via `fmt(sample.net)`. Computing sampleNet() by hand with the app's current defaults (baseRate=65.15 at line 2204, DIFF_DEFAULTS night=+$10/hr and weekend-day=+$11.5/hr at line 686, federal 12%, state 2.5%, FICA standard 7.65%, no pretax/posttax) gives gross = 3*(75.15*12) + 2*(76.65*12) + 1*(65.15*12) = 5326.80, and net = 5326.80 - (5326.80*0.0765 + 5326.80*0.12 + 5326.80*0.025) = 5326.80 - 1180.04 = 4146.76, i.e. fmt() would show $4,147 — not $3,951. The two numbers disagree by about $196 (≈5%) for what is presented as the exact same 72-hour, 6-shift schedule.
findings.failure: A brand-new visitor sees '$3,951' on the very first screen (framed as 'we do the messy math so the number's never a surprise'). If she continues through the full setup path (steps 1-3) without touching any rate, the 'done' screen a few taps later — using the same default rate and the same 72-hour/6-shift assumption — shows $4,147 instead. The app contradicts its own headline number within a single onboarding session, which is precisely the kind of surprise the product claims to eliminate.
findings.fix: Either compute the welcome-screen figure the same way sampleNet() does (call the existing sampleNet-equivalent logic against current default state, which is already in scope at obStep 0) so the two screens can never drift apart again, or replace the literal '$3,951' with a value that is verified to match sampleNet()'s output under the current defaults. Do not hand-tune the string again without re-deriving it — that is how it went stale.

findings.title: "Clear the sample" removes the seeded shifts but leaves the placeholder $65.15/hr rate in place with no indication it isn't real, once the honesty banner is gone
findings.where: index.html:2991-3000 (clearSample), index.html:3408-3412 (finish('sample')), index.html:2231 and 969 (estimateMode is the only signal that the rate is fake)
findings.detail: finish('sample') (line 3408-3412) sets `baseRate` to the placeholder 65.15 and seeds sample shifts, marking the state as fake only via `estimateMode:'sample'`. The est-banner (line 3464-3475) offers two exits when estimateMode==='sample': 'Enter my rate' (opens Settings) and 'Clear the sample' (calls `clearSample`). `clearSample` (line 2991-3000) strips the SAMPLE_PATTERN_ID-tagged shifts and unconditionally does `setEstimateMode('')` — it never checks whether the user actually entered a real base rate first. There is no other field anywhere (grep confirms `estimateMode` is the sole indicator) distinguishing 'nurse's real $65.15/hr' from 'never-touched placeholder $65.15/hr'.
findings.failure: A nurse taps 'Show me an example' to see how the app works, then taps 'Clear the sample' directly (never 'Enter my rate'). The seeded shifts vanish and the banner disappears — but baseRate is still the fictitious 65.15. Every shift she now logs herself computes gross/take-home/hero figures against that fake rate with no banner, no warning, and nothing in the UI distinguishing it from a confirmed real rate. This state also serializes into the cloud blob and localStorage (serializeState includes baseRate and estimateMode='' ), so it persists across sessions and devices silently. The app's headline numbers are now systematically wrong for her actual pay, with the one mechanism designed to flag that (the est-banner) already dismissed.
findings.fix: Track whether the base rate was ever explicitly set by the user (independent of estimateMode), or make `clearSample` refuse/redirect to rate entry when `baseRate` still equals the untouched sample default, so clearing the sample can never silently promote a placeholder rate to authoritative status.

findings.title: Editing a savings goal's target down to $0 in Settings makes the Add-Shift preview show "Infinity%"
findings.detail:
In Settings' SAVINGS GOALS list, each goal's target is edited with `<NumInput value={g.target} onCommit={v=>updGoalTarget(g.id,v)} min={0} .../>` (index.html:4754), and `updGoalTarget=(id,v)=>setGoals((goals||[]).map(g=> g.id===id ? {...g, target:parseFloat(v)||0} : g))` (index.html:4686) has no floor above 0. NumInput's own commit logic (index.html:4020-4028) sets the value to `min` (i.e. 0) whenever the field is cleared and blurred, or the user simply types 0. So a goal that already exists with a positive target can be driven to `target:0` entirely from the UI, live, in the same session — no reload and no pass through `sanitizeData` in between (Settings and AddShiftSheet share the exact same top-level `goals` state, wired at index.html:3617 and index.html:4677).

The forward per-shift preview at index.html:4247-4248 computes `const pct=Math.round(previewNet/g.target*1000)/10; const n=Math.ceil(g.target/previewNet);` guarded only by `previewNet>0` — there is no `g.target>0` check here (unlike the Settings reverse-view at index.html:4748, which does guard with `per>0 && g.target>0`, and unlike `sanitizeData`'s goals filter at index.html:1069-1081, which explicitly drops any goal whose `target` isn't a finite positive number specifically "so a malformed value can't yield NaN percentages in the shift preview"). With `g.target===0`, `previewNet/g.target` is `Infinity` in JS (positive/0), so `pct` is `Infinity` and the template literal renders the literal string "Infinity%".
findings.failure: 1) Open Settings → SAVINGS GOALS, tap into an existing goal's amount field, clear it (or type 0) and tap/tab away so it blurs — the goal's target silently becomes $0, with no error or warning. 2) Close Settings and open the Add-Shift sheet for any day with a shift that has nonzero take-home. The goal line at the bottom of the shift preview reads e.g. "toward your goal: House down payment Infinity% (≈0 shifts)" — a glaringly broken, alarming figure shown right next to the take-home dollar amount the app exists to make trustworthy.
findings.fix: Guard the AddShiftSheet goal line the same way the Settings reverse view already does — skip (or filter out) any goal whose `target` is not finite and > 0, e.g. change the `.map` at index.html:4248 to filter `goals.filter(g=>g.target>0)` before computing pct/n, or add `g.target>0 &&` inside the per-goal computation. Ideally also stop `updGoalTarget` from ever committing a non-positive target in the first place (e.g. clamp to the previous value, or require target>0 the same way `addGoal` already does at index.html:4684-4685), since that closes the root cause rather than just the one downstream symptom.

findings.title: Swap board lets a nurse commit to a shift with zero indication of what it pays
findings.where: index.html:3643 (SwapsSheet call site), 4819 (SwapsSheet signature), 5505-5531 (SUGGESTED FOR YOU cards), 5079-5099 (doPropose), 4067-4072 (giveMetaLine)
findings.detail:
SwapsSheet is invoked at index.html:3643 with `user, shifts, dayEvents, notes, saveDayShifts, differentials` — no `baseRate`, no `keepRatio`, no tax inputs. Compare the sibling sheets at the same call-site block: AddShiftSheet gets `baseRate={baseRate} keepRatio={keepRatio}` and PatternLab gets `baseRate={baseRate} taxes={taxInputs}`. SwapsSheet structurally cannot compute a dollar figure for anything it shows, because it was never given the numbers to do it with. Its own comment at giveMetaLine (4066: "wage-free by construction — shift_meta never carries $") makes this deliberate for the *data model* (correct: differing bonus/OT status shouldn't transfer between nurses), but it also blocks the client-side display, which has nothing to do with the anonymity model and could safely use the viewer's own baseRate/differentials the same way AddShiftSheet already does (previewGross/previewNet at 4104-4105).
The result: the 'SUGGESTED FOR YOU' cards (5505-5531) render PICK UP / TRADE / 3-WAY SHUFFLE suggestions as date + shift-type + hours only (`describeLeg`, 5509) and a bare 'Propose' button (5527) that calls doPropose (5079) straight into `proposeSwapMatch`, which freezes the posts. Nothing between seeing the suggestion and committing to it ever calls `shiftGross`/`computeNet` on the incoming shift.
findings.failure: A nurse opens Swaps, sees 'PICK UP · Fri Sep 19 · Night ×12h' and taps Propose. Once the other party accepts, the match is confirmed and effectively irreversible except through a Decline that the app itself frames as a social cost ('The others involved will see it fell through', 5155). Only after fully committing — accepting, revealing names, and tapping 'Add to my calendar' (doApplyPlan, 5260) — does she discover, via the Planner hero, what that shift actually pays. She had no way to compare this pickup against staying home, or against another posted shift, before agreeing to it. This directly contradicts the app's own stated promise, verbatim at the welcome screen ('Know your real take-home before you pick up the shift', line 5718) and the share blurb ('see what a shift is really worth before you pick it up', line 5667) — and it's inconsistent with the app's own established convention of surfacing $/hr specifically to 'compare pickups at a glance' (AddShiftSheet, line 4246), a convention the swap board's literal 'PICK UP' feature doesn't follow.
findings.fix: Pass `baseRate` and `keepRatio` (or the fuller `taxes`, matching PatternLab) into SwapsSheet, and render an estimated take-home (or at minimum ≈$/hr) on each suggestion card and open board post using the viewer's own rate — the same `shiftGross`/`computeNet` calls AddShiftSheet already makes, applied to `shift_meta` — before the Propose button, not after acceptance. This adds a new displayed dollar figure, so it should go through the wage-core protocol (baseline probes, a new assertion, the deployed-build equality check) even though it doesn't touch shiftGross/computeNet/calc themselves — flagging wageCore for that reason.
